ranking.note: Placed ahead of #35581 because it is the extracted base of both #35581 and #33922; reviewing it first unblocks the chain.
Moved up among P3s: it is the only actual user-visible bug fix (CHECK_NONFATAL on getblocktemplate/generateblock during shutdown), which outranks features and tests.

inconsistencies: Review chain: #35675 (BlockTemplateManager extraction) is the base for both #35581 (waitNext fee inflow) and #33922 (getMemoryLoad / template memory tracking). #35675 must be reviewed first; reviewing #35581 or #33922 ahead of it duplicates effort, since #35581's own manager code is the part extracted into #35675.
Partial overlap: #35581 and #35675 both add a 'block template manager'; #35675 is the agreed extraction, so #35581 should be read as the fee-inflow delta only.
#35598 was carved out of #33922 as out-of-scope test coverage; the two touch the same waitNext/feeThreshold behaviour and are best looked at together, with #33922 (after #35675) first.

#36097 depends on unmerged upstream bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess#342; its cancellation model would also change how #36192's 'IPC connection survives a failed createNewBlock' expectation is expressed, so #36097's approach decision should be settled before further interrupt-adjacent work lands.

#36132 and #36156 both change BlockAssembler/Mining edge-case semantics that reviewers themselves called theoretical or worth under 1000 sats; they sit correctly in P4 and should not displace the template-manager chain.
result.notes: Bands left as assessed; the list genuinely spans P2 (template-manager chain with concrete performance and unblocking payoff), P3 (one real bug fix, interface features, test coverage, regtest tooling) and P4 (theoretical or sub-1000-sat edge cases). Within P3 the ordering puts the bug fix and external-interface stability work ahead of added test coverage and developer tooling, per the category's 'template validity and correctness first, tooling last' ordering.
